THE RED SHAWL

INT. SMALL HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - MORNING

A cramped room with a sewing machine by the window. MOHAN (55), a retired clerk, sorts papers at a low table. His daughter KAVITA (24) stands at the door in a GREEN SUIT, holding a thin invitation card.

KAVITA
Papa, the wedding is on Sunday. You said you would come.

MOHAN
I said I would think about it.

KAVITA
Thinking has taken three months.

The old man does not look up. Kavita places the CARD on the table, its edge printed with the name M. RAO. She leaves.

EXT. NARROW LANE OUTSIDE THE HOUSE - DAY

Kavita walks fast. Their neighbour SUMAN (40) calls from a doorway and hurries over with a folded RED SHAWL.

SUMAN
Your mother wore this at her own wedding. Take it.

KAVITA
Aunty, I cannot.

SUMAN
You can. And you will.

Kavita takes the shawl. Her ankle turns on a broken step and she scrapes her right knee. Suman kneels and presses a cloth to the cut.

INT. TAILOR SHOP - AFTERNOON

BHATT (60), the tailor, measures Kavita, who now wears a YELLOW SUIT and a bandage on her knee. The shawl lies over a chair.

BHATT
Your father came here last week. He asked for a coat to be altered.

KAVITA
A coat? For what?

BHATT
He did not say. He paid in advance.

Kavita stares at the shawl. She says nothing.

INT. SMALL HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mohan sits alone, the RED SHAWL in his lap, the CARD beside him. Kavita enters, still in the yellow suit.

MOHAN
Bhatt told you.

KAVITA
He did not have to.

Mohan holds out the shawl. She takes it and drapes it over his shoulders. Neither speaks. The sewing machine ticks in the dark.
